description:
Functional specifications covered with associated files to edit/add: lib/zaq/accounts/people.ex, person_merger.ex, Connect-owned transactional transfer/cleanup helpers and Person grant/attempt schema constraints; test/zaq/accounts/* existing merge/deletion tests plus Connect concurrency cases. Accounts orchestrates identity lifecycle; Connect owns grant queries, collision rules, encrypted material handling and mutation jobs. Extend existing PersonMerger transaction/advisory-lock convention; do not create a second merge transaction. For each credential, transfer loser-only current grant to survivor; survivor-only unchanged; when both have rows retain survivor regardless of active/revoked/expired status and remove loser secret. Never overwrite survivor secret; retaining revoked survivor preserves explicit opt-out. Update polymorphic owner_id atomically and avoid decrypt/re-encrypt unless required. Revoke/cancel pending OAuth attempts for merged/deleted initiators rather than allowing callback to write survivor credentials implicitly. Permanently deleting Person deletes owned grants/secrets and pending attempts transactionally, including bulk deletion; produce safe events for former owner and survivor/credential dependencies as relevant before IDs disappear. Account for active executions using global fallback when a transferred grant becomes available: notify survivor even when no survivor grant existed.

Tests to add before implementation: loser-only, survivor-only, both rows for each status class; multiple credentials and multiple losers; survivor revoked versus loser active; no secret overwrite; delete and bulk delete; failed merge rollback preserves grants and emits no job; concurrent grant issue/refresh/OAuth callback against merge/delete; current Person validation and canonical unique constraints remain satisfied; transferred grant cannot be resolved for deleted loser. Test stale authenticated alias/session cannot gain survivor grant management by normalization alone.

Branches/paths validated: missing Person, merged aliases, duplicate merge request, collision across legacy and canonical grants. Decide legacy person-owned resource rows are prohibited in this slice so no unhandled orphan ownership lane. Use same deterministic lock order across canonical mutation and PersonMerger paths; explicitly test deadlock-sensitive interleavings. No People module query of token payloads; no secret values passed into lifecycle notifications. Explicit transactional cleanup/merge precedes parent deletion and emits notifications. No Person FK/RESTRICT triggers or coordination guard rows: residual concurrent orphans are accepted and require reconciliation.

Mocking plan: no internal mocks; real Repo/merge orchestration/Oban; independent transaction concurrency harness. Documentations to update: Accounts and Connect moduledocs, docs/services/engine.md Person lifetime ownership and stale-session rule, relevant identity documentation located during implementation. Coordinate existing merge coverage debt zaq-c1k without silently expanding unrelated work. >=95% touched-file coverage or measured explicit exception and follow-up.

COHESIVE LIFECYCLE IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENT (dependent on existing foundation steps): implement Connect-owned orphan-secret reconciliation invoked by a bounded worker/maintenance entry point. Select canonical person grants whose literal owner no longer exists, in stable grant-ID keyset batches with explicit batch limit and continuation, and delete orphan rows including encrypted material without decrypting. Recheck orphan status at deletion, preserve valid owners and all legacy org/user grants, and handle retries/concurrent cleanup idempotently. Never follow merged aliases or reassign orphan credentials implicitly. Reconcile pending OAuth attempts as applicable. Tests BEFORE implementation: direct and concurrent orphan creation, full encrypted-row removal, valid-owner preservation, stale alias survivor untouched, batch boundaries and deterministic ordering, continuation/restart, repeated runs returning no further deletions, failure rollback, concurrent cleanup, secret-free telemetry and safe events. Telemetry allowlists counts/outcomes/duration only, never secret payloads/raw structs/metadata or owner-identifying high-cardinality labels. Record the non-reuse assumption and lack of synchronous erasure guarantee in operational docs. This implementation is later work and has NOT shipped with storage.

2026-09-14 FINAL USER-APPROVED STORAGE DECISION: canonical grants reuse owner_type/owner_id (org with NULL ID or person with non-null ID) and resource_type=connect_credential/resource_id=credential_id string. Native type/shape and explicit non-null/equality CHECKs plus existing credential_id FK; partial unique org/person slots across statuses. No binding_type, duplicate person_id, extra Person FK, triggers or guard rows. Server derives resource pair and configuration auth fields; secret_binding stays independent. Trusted canonical storage checks literal current active Person, without authenticating callers or resolving aliases. Concurrent orphan grants/secrets are an accepted residual risk. IDs must not be reused operationally; no silent reidentification through stale aliases; synchronous erasure is not guaranteed. Later resolver must check Person exists/eligible BEFORE policy selection even disabled, and missing/stale Person errors NEVER fall back globally. Authenticated writes and OAuth/refresh must recheck current identity; lifecycle cleanup/reconciliation and later distributed server invalidation remain unimplemented in storage task .1.
title: [zaq-jrg.8] 8. Integrate Person grant cleanup and deterministic merge
